headline: Minimal and spatial models link cell-scale rules to population-level outcomes
label: Mathematical Models Of Cell Dynamics
summary: Reduced and spatially resolved models now connect individual cell behavior, lesion patterns, and hypoxic growth switching to population-level outcomes.
synthesis: The common thread is the use of minimal or spatially resolved mathematical models to connect cell-scale rules with population-level behavior. A two-phenotype go-or-grow tumor model under cyclic hypoxia is reduced to a single oxygen-dependent equation and checked against numerical simulations. A kinetic reaction-diffusion model of demyelinating lesions is analyzed through Turing and weakly nonlinear methods, with simulations as verification. A CompuCell3D agent-based model of tuberculosis granuloma progression is compared with a prior within-host model. In bacterial communities, agent-based simulations and a drift-diffusion model indicate that cell morphology and division rate govern fixation in dual populations. What is new is the explicit linkage of individual-level morphology, phenotypic switching, or lesion-scale pattern formation to population outcome, with analytical reduction offered as an interpretable route.
